answer 1. I got the Sithis beard without trouble from the crocodiles. Weeltul, tree-minder of Jal-Veesa, wants it. The Hist is the town great tree in a pool. 2. Take the beard to Weeltul at the Hist pool in the middle of Jal-Veesa, east along the road. 3. Go straight there; I could also talk to people in town first. 4. I still do not know why Vosh-Leera wants me, or what the Owing is. I could ask townsfolk.

answer 1. The Hist of Jal-Veesa is sick: dry dark bark, closed scar, cooling egg-pool. Weeltul does not know why. If it dies no eggs hatch and the town empties in a generation. The moss only helps briefly. 2. Speak to Vosh-Leera in her house in Jal-Veesa. 3. Talk to Vosh-Leera now, or first ask Weeltul about the sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel. 4. I do not know what Umbriel is, what the sap and scar mean in full, or why Vosh-Leera wants me. I can ask Weeltul and Vosh-Leera.

answer 1. I am Tarin, a thief freed from the Owing barge. Vosh-Leera, root-herald of Jal-Veesa, freed me because she works for the Toh-Reel-Ka, the Secret Warriors of the Xeech-Leel, who rule the province. Trees (Hists) along the river are falling sick and nobody knows why. Jal-Veesa Hist is dry, its scar closed, its egg-pool cooling. They want the cause found and chose me because I am a stranger with no kin. 2. Ask Vosh-Leera for the second task in her house in Jal-Veesa. 3. Take the task, or first ask Weeltul about the sap, scar, eggs and Umbriel. I do not know yet if I can refuse. 4. I do not know why the trees are sick, or what the second task is. I can ask Vosh-Leera and Weeltul. Notes for a friend: I have 50 gold, a lockpick, and the Hist blessing (resist poison). I got the moss from the weir without fighting the crocodiles. Weeltul is at the Hist pool. Vosh-Leera is in Jal-Veesa, with her house door nearby.
